title: What kind of triangle has these three sides?
description: Each set of three sides is first checked to make a real triangle. Then the equal sides are counted: three equal, two equal, or none equal. Keeko's doubt is that two equal sides are enough to call a triangle equilateral.
teaching_notes: One idea: count the equal sides to name the kind of triangle after checking that it exists. Watch for students who call a triangle with two equal sides equilateral.

source: Equilateral triangles have sides of equal length. Isosceles triangles have two sides of equal length. Scalene triangles have sides of three different lengths.
video_script.why: The child knows the triangle inequality and has met triangles with equal sides, and now names a triangle from its side lengths.
video_script.substitution: Three sets of sides: 5 cm, 5 cm, 5 cm; 5 cm, 5 cm, 8 cm; and 5 cm, 6 cm, 7 cm.
video_script.anchor: three triangles with sides marked in centimetres
video_script.wrong_answer: two equal sides make a triangle equilateral
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees two equal sides in the second triangle and calls it equilateral, but equilateral needs all three sides equal and the third side is eight centimetres.
video_script.payoff_line: They are equilateral, isosceles and scalene

final_answer.spoken: they are equilateral, isosceles and scalene

maths_rules: a triangle exists when the longest side is less than the sum of the other two: 5 < 5 + 5, 8 < 5 + 5, 7 < 5 + 6
video_script.design: Three triangles stay on the board with their sides marked. Equal sides carry matching tick marks, and the count of equal sides is written under each triangle.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the sides of triangles.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first triangle has sides of five, five and five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second has sides of five, five and eight.
<bookmark mark='third'/>The third has sides of five, six and seven.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We have to name the kind of each triangle.

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Sides can be all the same length, and equal sides carry the same tick mark.

<bookmark mark='diff'/>Sometimes no two sides match at all, and every side is different.

beats.on_screen: Given: sides (a) 5 cm, 5 cm, 5 cm  (b) 5 cm, 5 cm, 8 cm  (c) 5 cm, 6 cm, 7 cm

marks.given: the three sets of sides are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three sets of sides, first, second and third.

marks.find: the question is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to name each triangle, after checking that it really exists.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the longest side must be less than the sum of the other two: 5 < 5 + 5 = 10;  8 < 5 + 5 = 10;  7 < 5 + 6 = 11

marks.rule: the rule about the longest side is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, the longest side must be less than the sum of the other two.
<bookmark mark='one'/>For the first, five is less than five plus five, which is ten.
<bookmark mark='two'/>For the second, eight is less than ten.
<bookmark mark='three'/>For the third, seven is less than five plus six, which is eleven. All three triangles exist.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the first triangle, 5, 5, 5: all three sides are equal

marks.first: the first triangle lights up with the same tick on all three sides
marks.count: the words all three sides equal are written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, count the equal sides of the first triangle.
<bookmark mark='count'/>All three sides are equal, so the same tick sits on each.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the second, 5, 5, 8: exactly two sides equal;  the third, 5, 6, 7: all three sides different

marks.second: the second triangle lights up with a tick on two sides and none on the third
marks.two: the words exactly two sides equal are written
marks.third: the third triangle lights up with no matching ticks
marks.none: the words all three sides different are written

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step three, the second triangle has two sides of five.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Exactly two sides are equal, and the third is longer.
<bookmark mark='third'/>In the third, the sides are five, six and seven.
<bookmark mark='none'/>All three sides are different, so none of them match.

marks.eq: the word equilateral appears under the first triangle
marks.iso: the word isosceles appears under the second triangle
marks.sca: the word scalene appears under the third triangle

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>They are equilateral, isosceles and scalene.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>A triangle with three equal sides is called equilateral.
<bookmark mark='iso'/>A triangle with exactly two equal sides is called isosceles.
<bookmark mark='sca'/>A triangle with three different sides is called scalene.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks two equal sides make a triangle equilateral.

<bookmark mark='kind'/>Two equal sides make a different kind of triangle.
